discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave photons
motivation: The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum behaviour in Josephson circuits. The next step was circuit quantum electrodynamics (circuit QED). Blais proposed it theoretically in 2004, and Wallraff, Schoelkopf and co-workers realised it the same year: they put a superconducting qubit inside a microwave resonator and reached strong coupling between one artificial atom and one photon. Experiments in Paris and elsewhere had shown cavity QED with real atoms. Circuit QED moved it onto a chip, with coupling strengths and design freedom that atoms cannot offer. It made quantum non-demolition dispersive readout, photon-mediated qubit-qubit gates and bus architectures possible, and it shaped the transmon, which suppressed charge noise and took coherence from nanoseconds to milliseconds. Bosonic codes, microwave quantum optics and the recent demonstrations of error correction below threshold all build on this framework. Today almost every superconducting quantum processor is a circuit-QED device.
